facts.statement: Caseodus lived during the Carboniferous period in what is now the Midwestern United States and potentially the Early Triassic in what is now British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: Caseodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont from the Carboniferous of what is now the Midwestern United States, and potentially the Early Triassic of what is now British Columbia, Canada.

facts.statement: The genus name honors paleoichthyologist Gerard Case, and the type species was originally classified in the genus Orodus.
facts.quote: The genus name is in honor of paleoichthyologist Gerard Case, and the type species was originally placed in the genus Orodus.

facts.statement: All species of Caseodus grew to approximately 1 to 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: All species in the genus grew to approximately 1 - 1.5 m in length.

facts.statement: The Triassic species of Caseodus completely lacked upper jaws and featured an elongated projection called a rostrum extending from the lower jaw to support the tooth-whorl.
facts.quote: The Triassic species entirely lacked upper jaws and had an elongated projection, termed a rostrum, which extended from the lower jaw and supported the lower tooth-whorl.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Early Triassic species C. varidentis belongs in the genus Caseodus due to its significantly different skull and tooth morphology.
facts.quote: A third species, C. varidentis, is known from the Early Triassic Sulphur Mountain Formation, but due to its wildly different skull and tooth morphology it is questionable if it belongs in the genus.

facts.statement: Caseodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Eugeneodontiformes that lived during the Carboniferous period.
facts.quote: Caseodus es un género extinto de peces cartilaginosos del orden Eugeneodontiformes que vivieron en el período Carbonífero.

facts.statement: Caseodus is classified within the family Caseodontidae.
The genus Caseodus was described by Zangerl in 1981.
The parent group of the genus Caseodus is the family Caseodontidae.

rejected.statement: Carboniferous species of Caseodus possessed upper jaws supporting teeth and a row of fused teeth called a tooth-whorl along the midline of the lower jaw.
rejected.quote: The Carboniferous species had upper jaws which supported teeth and a row of fused teeth (termed a tooth-whorl) along the midline of the lower jaw.
